# Problem 1

## a. For the waldCI class, define some followings

```{r}
setClass("waldCI",
          slots = c(level = "numeric",
                    mean = "numeric",
                    sterr = "numeric"))
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {
 if (object@level <= 0 | object@level >= 1) {
 stop("level must be in (0, 1)")
 }
 if (object@sterr <= 0) {
 stop("stderr must be positive")
 }
 if (!is.finite(object@sterr)) {
 stop("Infinite CI not supported")
 }
 return(TRUE)
})
```

```{r}
#' Title Create `waldCI` object.
#' @param level 
#' @param lb 
#' @param ub 
#' @param mean 
#' @param sterr 
#' @returns A `waldCI` object
#' @export
makeCI <- function(level,
                   lb = NULL,
                   ub = NULL,
                   mean = NULL,
                   sterr = NULL) {
 if (!is.null(mean) && !is.null(stderr) &&
      is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)) {
   return(new("waldCI", level = level, mean = mean, sterr = sterr))
 } else if (is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr) &&
            !is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub)) {
 if (lb > ub) {
   stop("lb must be less than ub")
 }
 z <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2)
 mean <- (lb + ub) / 2
 sterr <- (ub - lb) / (2 * z)
 return(new("waldCI", level = level, mean = mean, sterr = sterr))
 } else {
   stop("Input must be either lb/ub or mean/sterr")
 }
}
```

method:

```{r}
#' Title Internal function to compute bounds
#' @param ci 
#' @returns A
#' @export
.getBounds <- function(ci) {
  z <- qnorm((1 + ci@level)/2)
  lb <- ci@mean - z*ci@sterr
  ub <- ci@mean + z*ci@sterr
  return(c(lb, ub))
}

#' Title Show method for waldCI object
#' @param waldCI 
#' @returns `object`, invisibly
#' @export
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
 bound <- .getBounds(object)
 cat(round(object@level*100))
 cat("% CI: (")
 cat(bound[1])
 cat(", ")
 cat(bound[2])
 cat(")\n")
 return(invisible(object))
})
```

Accessors:

```{r}
#' Title Internal function to get a named slot
#' @param object 
#' @param slotname 
#' @returns A
#' @export
.getSlot <- function(object, slotname) {
 if (slotname %in% c("level", "mean", "sterr")) {
    return(slot(object, slotname))
 }
 bounds <- .getBounds(object)
 if (slotname == "lb") {
   return(bounds[1])
 } else if (slotname == "ub") {
   return(bounds[2])
 } else {
   stop("Invalid slotname")
 }
}

#' Title Getters and Setters for Wald CI objects
#' @param object A `waldCI` object
#' @returns Getters return scalar; setters return the object
#' @export
setGeneric("level", function(object) {standardGeneric("level")})
```

contains and overlaps:

```{r}
##' Check whether a CI overlaps with a constant or another CI
##' (`overlap`)
##' @param ci A `waldCI` object
##' @param value A numeric value
##' @return Logical.
##' @rdname contains_overlaps
##' @export
contains <- function(ci, value) {
 stopifnot(is.numeric(value))
 stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
 bounds <- .getBounds(ci)
 return(value > bounds[1] & value < bounds[2])
}

##' @param ci1 
##' @param ci2 
##' @rdname contains_overlaps
##' @export
overlap <- function(ci1, ci2) {
 b1 <- .getBounds(ci1)
 b2 <- .getBounds(ci2)
 return(max(b1[1], b2[1]) <= min(b1[2], b2[2]))
}
```

as.numeric:

```{r}
##' Convert waldCI to numeric
##' @return Length 2 vector of the bounds of `x`.
##' @export
setGeneric("as.numeric")
setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x) {
 return(.getBounds(x))
})
```

Transform:

```{r}
##' Apply a monotonic transformation to a `waldCI`
##' @param ci A `waldCI` object
##' @param fn Any function that takes in a scalar and returns a scalar.
##' @return The transformed waldCI
##' @export
transformCI <- function(ci, fn) {
 stopifnot(is.function(fn))
 stopifnot(is(ci, "waldCI"))
 return(makeCI(level = ci@level,
 mean = fn(ci@mean),
 sterr = fn(ci@sterr)))
}
```

# Problem 2

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nzelect)
library(data.table)
tennis <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azhou5849/tennis-atp-sackmann-data/master/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
setDT(tennis)
```

## a. How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
tennis[, .(1), tourney_name][, .(.N)]

tennis[, tourney_name2 := fifelse(grepl("^Davis", tourney_name), "Davis", tourney_name)] |>
  _[, .(1), tourney_name2] |>
  _[, .(.N)]
```

## b. Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
tennis[order(tourney_name, -match_num), .(winner_name, match_num, tourney_name)] |>
  _[, .SD[1], by = tourney_name] |>
  _[, .(winner_name, .N), winner_name] |>
  _[order(-N),] |>
  _[1:3]
```

```{r}
tennis[round == "F", .(N = .N), winner_name] |>
  _[order(-N),] |>
  _[1:3]
```

## c. Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers?

```{r}
stats <- tennis[, .(winmore = w_ace > l_ace)] |>
  _[!is.na(winmore),.(x = sum(winmore), n = .N), ,]
prop.test(stats$x, stats$n, .5)
```

## d. Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
tennis[, .(player = c(winner_name, loser_name), winloss = c(rep(1, .N), rep(0, .N)))] |>
  _[, .(winrate = mean(winloss), games = .N), player] |>
  _[games >= 5, .(player, winrate)] |>
  _[order(-winrate)] |>
  _[1:3]
```

# Problem 3

```{r}
library(plotly)
covid <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv")
covid$date <- lubridate::ymd(covid$date)
names(covid)[names(covid) == "date"] <- "Date"
names(covid)[names(covid) == "state"] <- "State"
```

## a. How many major and minor spikes in cases were there?

```{r}
plot_ly(covid, x = ~ Date, y = ~ cases_avg, type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines") %>%
 layout(yaxis = list(title = "Daily Cases"))
```

## b. For the states with the highest and lowest overall rates per population, what differences do you see in their trajectories over time?

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)
```

```{r}
state_case_rate <- covid %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarise(cumulative_rate = sum(cases_avg_per_100k), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(cumulative_rate))

state_highest_rate <- state_case_rate$State[1]
state_lowest_rate  <- state_case_rate$State[nrow(state_case_rate)]

covid_merged <- covid %>%
  inner_join(state_case_rate, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(State = factor(State, levels = state_case_rate$State))

all_states <- levels(covid_merged$State)

state_colors <- rep("lightgrey", length(all_states))

state_colors[all_states == state_lowest_rate] <- "red"
state_colors[all_states == state_highest_rate] <- "blue"

rate_plot <- plot_ly(covid_merged, 
                     x = ~ Date, 
                     y = ~ cases_avg_per_100k,
                     color = ~ State,
                     colors = state_colors,
                     type = "scatter",
                     mode = "lines") %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(title = "7-day Average COVID Cases per 100k Residents"))

all_state_labels <- levels(covid_merged$State)
traces_to_hide <- which(!(all_state_labels %in% c(state_highest_rate, state_lowest_rate)))

rate_plot <- style(rate_plot, visible = "legendonly", traces = traces_to_hide)
rate_plot

```

## c. Identify, to the best of your ability without a formal test, the first five states to experience Covid in a substantial way.

```{r}
library(lubridate)
```

```{r}
selected_states <- c(
  "New York", "New Jersey", "Louisiana",
  "Guam", "Massachusetts", "Rhode Island"
)

highlight_data <- covid %>%
  filter(State %in% selected_states) %>%
  mutate(State = factor(State, levels = selected_states))

other_data <- covid %>%
  filter(!State %in% selected_states)

# Colors for the selected states
state_palette <- c(
  "red", "blue", "green",
  "purple", "orange", "yellow"
)

rate_plot <- plot_ly() %>%

  add_lines(
    data = other_data,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
    split = ~State,
    line = list(color = "lightgrey", width = 0.7),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    hoverinfo = "skip"
  ) %>%

  add_lines(
    data = highlight_data,
    x = ~Date,
    y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
    color = ~State,
    colors = state_palette,
    line = list(width = 2.5),
    text = ~paste0(
      State,
      "<br>Date: ", Date,
      "<br>Cases per 100k: ",
      round(cases_avg_per_100k, 1)
    ),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%

  layout(
    title = "Early COVID-19 Trends in Selected States",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Date",
      range = c("2020-03-01", "2020-05-31")
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Daily Cases per 100,000",
      range = c(0, 55)
    )
  )

rate_plot
```
